notes: This contract pins Umbra's opt-in, non-installable embedded time-advance development slice to source-derived IEEE 1516.1-2025 records. The slice initializes each joined federate at the selected representation's initial time, retains a Time Advance Request until the configured callback dispatcher delivers Time Advance Grant, records the accepted request to the selected filesystem before that callback, and exposes Query Logical Time. Regional interaction and object-attribute TSO companions additionally prove that ordinary TAR and NMR grants deliver the overlap-qualified callback before the grant at the inclusive timestamp frontier. A default-source timestamped attribute-update companion adds one producer TAR to the shared FQR/TARA/NMRA frontier and proves its grant completes independently after the three default-region reflections. A separate contract traces the limited no-TSO GALT/NRG scheduler that can release TAR callbacks across federates. The restore-control contract has narrow process-local regressions for a saved current time, a deferred lookahead decrease, paired HLA_EVOKED/HLA_IMMEDIATE pending NRG TAR, HLA_EVOKED pending FQR, and a six-scenario TARA/NMR/NMRA matrix under both callback models. They do not establish complete save/restore semantics for time management. Separate timestamped/TSO contracts cover bounded queue behavior; selected queued/in-transit restore, broader coordination, package support, catalog result, JUnit sidecar, protected review, and conformance remain open.
